nodes.summary: For every x-fast trie $t$ over $w$-bit keys and every $w$-bit key $x$, the set of keys stored in the trie obtained by inserting $x$ into $t$ is the set of keys stored in $t$ with $x$ added.
nodes.title: Keys of an x-fast trie after insertion

nodes.summary: Let $t$ be a y-fast trie over $w$-bit keys, let $R$ be the set of keys stored in the representative x-fast trie of $t$, and for each $r \in R$ let $B(r)$ be the bucket owned by $r$. The set of keys stored in $t$ is the union of the buckets of its representatives, $\bigcup_{r \in R} B(r)$.
nodes.title: Keys of a y-fast trie

nodes.summary: The empty x-fast trie over $w$-bit keys stores no keys, and the prefix set at each of its levels $0, 1, \dots, w$ is empty.
nodes.title: The empty x-fast trie

nodes.summary: Let $t$ be a valid x-fast trie over $w$-bit keys, let $0 \le l \le w$ and let $x$ be a $w$-bit key. The probe of level $l$ of $t$ at $x$ succeeds if and only if some key $y$ stored in $t$ has the same $l$-bit prefix as $x$.
nodes.title: Level probes of a valid x-fast trie

nodes.summary: For an x-fast trie $t$ over $w$-bit keys, a level $0 \le l \le w$ and a $w$-bit key $x$, the probe of level $l$ of $t$ at $x$ returns true exactly when the $l$-bit prefix of $x$ belongs to the prefix set stored at level $l$ of $t$.
nodes.title: Level probe of an x-fast trie

nodes.summary: Inserting a $w$-bit key $x$ into an x-fast trie $t$ adds $x$ to the keys stored in $t$ and, for each level $0 \le l \le w$, adds the $l$-bit prefix of $x$ to the prefix set at level $l$.
nodes.title: Insertion into an x-fast trie

nodes.summary: If $t$ is a valid y-fast trie over $w$-bit keys, then a $w$-bit key $x$ is stored in $t$ if and only if $x$ lies in the bucket owned by some $w$-bit key $r$ (such an owner $r$ is then necessarily a representative).
nodes.title: Keys of a valid y-fast trie are the keys in buckets

nodes.summary: For every y-fast trie $t$ over $w$-bit keys and every $w$-bit key $x$, $x$ is stored in $t$ if and only if $x$ lies in the bucket owned by some representative of $t$, that is, by some key stored in the representative x-fast trie of $t$.
nodes.title: Membership in a y-fast trie via representatives' buckets

nodes.summary: For a valid x-fast trie $t$ over $w$-bit keys and a $w$-bit key $x$, the membership test of $t$ at $x$, which probes the deepest level $w$, returns true if and only if $x$ is stored in $t$.
nodes.title: The membership test of a valid x-fast trie is exact

nodes.summary: For every x-fast trie $t$ over $w$-bit keys and every $w$-bit key $x$, the membership test at $x$ of the trie obtained by inserting $x$ into $t$ returns true.
nodes.title: An inserted key passes the membership test

nodes.summary: For an x-fast trie $t$ over $w$-bit keys and a key $x < 2^w$, the membership query of $x$ in $t$ answers true exactly when the length-$w$ prefix of $x$, which is $x$ itself, lies in the prefix set that $t$ stores for level $w$: a single probe of the deepest level, as in the classical structure.
nodes.title: Membership query in an x-fast trie

nodes.summary: For an x-fast trie $t$ over $w$-bit keys and a key $x < 2^w$, the predecessor query of $x$ in $t$ returns no key if and only if no key stored in $t$ is smaller than $x$.
nodes.title: When an x-fast trie has no predecessor

nodes.summary: For an x-fast trie $t$ over $w$-bit keys and keys $x, y < 2^w$, the predecessor query of $x$ in $t$ returns $y$ if and only if $y$ is stored in $t$, $y < x$, and every key $z$ stored in $t$ with $z < x$ satisfies $z \le y$.
nodes.title: Characterization of the x-fast trie predecessor

nodes.summary: For an x-fast trie $t$ over $w$-bit keys and a key $x < 2^w$, the predecessor of $x$ in $t$ is the greatest key stored in $t$ that is smaller than $x$, if such a key exists; otherwise the query returns no key.
nodes.title: Predecessor query in an x-fast trie

nodes.summary: For every $w$-bit key $x < 2^w$, the length-$w$ prefix of $x$ equals $x$.
nodes.title: The full-length prefix of a key is the key

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $l \le w$ and a $w$-bit key $x < 2^w$, the length-$l$ prefix of $x$ is less than $2^l$.
nodes.title: A prefix fits in its length

nodes.summary: For every $w$-bit key $x < 2^w$, the length-$0$ prefix of $x$ (the trie root) is $0$.
nodes.title: The empty prefix is zero

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $l$ and $w$ and a $w$-bit key $x < 2^w$, the length-$l$ prefix of $x$ is the natural number $\lfloor x / 2^{w-l} \rfloor$, where $w - l$ is truncated subtraction (it is $0$ when $l > w$). For $l \le w$ these are the top $l$ bits of $x$, a number below $2^l$.
nodes.title: Bit prefix of a key

nodes.summary: If a y-fast trie $t$ over $w$-bit keys is valid, then every key of the representative x-fast trie of $t$ is a stored key of $t$.
nodes.title: Representatives of a valid y-fast trie are stored keys

nodes.summary: For an x-fast trie $t$ over $w$-bit keys and a key $x < 2^w$, the successor query of $x$ in $t$ returns no key if and only if no key stored in $t$ is greater than $x$.
nodes.title: When an x-fast trie has no successor

nodes.summary: Let $t$ be an x-fast trie over $w$-bit keys and let $x$ and $y$ be keys in $\{0, \dots, 2^w - 1\}$. The successor of $x$ in $t$ exists and equals $y$ if and only if $y$ is a stored key of $t$, $x < y$, and $y \le z$ for every stored key $z$ of $t$ with $x < z$.
nodes.title: Characterization of the x-fast trie successor

nodes.summary: For an x-fast trie $t$ over $w$-bit keys and a key $x \in \{0, \dots, 2^w - 1\}$, the successor of $x$ in $t$ is the least stored key of $t$ that is greater than $x$ when some stored key is greater than $x$; otherwise $x$ has no successor in $t$.
nodes.title: Successor in an x-fast trie

nodes.summary: A y-fast trie skeleton $t$ over $w$-bit keys, with bucket $B_r$ owned by each key $r$, is valid when its representative x-fast trie is valid, a key $r$ is stored in the representative x-fast trie exactly when its bucket $B_r$ is nonempty, and every key $r$ stored in the representative x-fast trie lies in its own bucket $B_r$.
nodes.title: Valid y-fast trie skeleton

nodes.summary: For every $w$, the empty x-fast trie over $w$-bit keys, which has no stored keys and every level empty, is valid.
nodes.title: The empty x-fast trie is valid

nodes.summary: If $t$ is a valid x-fast trie over $w$-bit keys and $x \in \{0, \dots, 2^w - 1\}$, then the x-fast trie obtained from $t$ by inserting $x$ is valid.
nodes.title: Insertion preserves validity of an x-fast trie

nodes.summary: An x-fast trie $t$ over $w$-bit keys is valid when, for every level $l \in \{0, \dots, w\}$, the level-$l$ set of $t$ equals the set of $l$-bit prefixes (top $l$ bits) of the stored keys of $t$.
nodes.title: Valid x-fast trie

nodes.summary: An x-fast trie over $w$-bit keys consists of a finite set of stored keys in $\{0, \dots, 2^w - 1\}$ together with, for each level $l \in \{0, \dots, w\}$, a finite set of natural numbers, intended to hold the $l$-bit prefixes of the stored keys.
nodes.title: x-fast trie

nodes.summary: A y-fast trie skeleton over $w$-bit keys consists of an x-fast trie over $w$-bit keys, whose stored keys are the representatives, together with a bucket $B_r$, a finite set of keys, for every key $r \in \{0, \dots, 2^w - 1\}$.
nodes.title: y-fast trie skeleton
